name: NAMASTE
title: NAMASTE — National Ayush Morbidity & Standardized Terminologies Electronic (SAMPLE)
description: SAMPLE — illustrative, not official. Codes prefixed SAMPLE- are not real NAMASTE or WHO codes. Ayush diagnosis codes with IAST, Devanagari, English and Hinglish designations.

concept.definition: Disease in which vitiated vata carries ama to the joints, producing pain, swelling and stiffness.
Vata disorder localised in the joints, with pain on movement and crepitus.
Disease of vitiated vata and rakta, beginning in the small joints of the feet.
Pain radiating from the buttock along the back of the thigh and leg.
Pain in the lumbar region.
Loss of function of one half of the body.
Deviation of one half of the face.
Stiffness and restricted movement of the neck.
Disorder of pitta with sour belching, heartburn and nausea.
Disorder of the grahani with alternating loose and hard stools, due to weak agni.
Frequent passage of loose watery stools.
Fleshy growths in the anal canal that obstruct the passage.
Incomplete digestion of ingested food.
Expulsion of stomach contents through the mouth.
Distension of the abdomen with obstruction of faeces and flatus.
Infestation by worms.
Expulsion of air from the respiratory passage with a characteristic sound.
Episodic breathlessness with wheeze, worse at night and in cold weather.
Nasal discharge with sneezing and heaviness of the head.
Repeated involuntary spasm of the diaphragm with a characteristic sound.
Progressive wasting of the body tissues.
Painful and difficult urination.
Stone formation in the urinary tract.
Obstruction to the flow of urine.
Skin disease with large, dry, scaly patches resembling fish scales.
Itchy skin eruption with discharge and dark discolouration.
White depigmented patches of the skin.
Sudden itchy wheals on the skin, often after exposure to cold wind.
Rapidly spreading inflammation of the skin.
Pallor of the skin with fatigue due to depletion of rakta.
Yellow discolouration of the eyes, skin and urine.
Bleeding from the upper or lower passages due to vitiated pitta.
Derangement of mind, intellect and behaviour.
Episodic loss of consciousness with abnormal movements.
Inability to obtain adequate sleep.
Painful menstruation.
White discharge per vaginum.
Excessive or prolonged menstrual bleeding.
Raised body temperature with discomfort of body and mind.
Fever of vata type, with irregular onset, body ache and dryness.
Fever of pitta type, with high temperature, burning and thirst.
Fever of kapha type, with heaviness, mild temperature and loss of appetite.
Group of disorders with excessive and turbid urination.
Type of prameha in which the urine is sweet like honey.
Excessive accumulation of meda (fat) in the body.
Swelling in the front of the neck.
Pain in the head.
Paroxysmal pain in one half of the head.
Group of disorders caused predominantly by vitiated vata.
Group of disorders of the gastrointestinal channel.
Group of disorders of the respiratory channel.
Group of disorders of the urinary channel.
Group of disorders of the skin.
Group of disorders of the blood-carrying channel.
Group of disorders of the mind-carrying channel.
Group of disorders of the menstrual channel.
Group of disorders of the fat-carrying channel.
Group of patterns of dosha imbalance.
Group of disorders of the head.
Pattern of increased vata, with dryness, roughness, pain and constipation.
Pattern of increased pitta, with burning, yellowish discolouration and thirst.
Pattern of increased kapha, with heaviness, lethargy and excess mucus.
Pattern in which the doshas are associated with ama, with heaviness, coated tongue and anorexia.
Pattern of diminished digestive fire, with poor appetite and slow digestion.
